subject: History
examFormat: Two compulsory papers taken as a composite at one sitting. Paper 1 (West Africa and the Wider World from the earliest times to 2000, for all candidates): fifty multiple-choice items, all answered in 1 hour for 40 marks. Paper 2 (national histories): a 2-hour essay test with sections A (earliest times to 1800), B (19th century) and C (1900-2000), each with three questions; candidates answer four questions on their own country, at least one from each section, for 60 marks.
excluded: The national-history sections for The Gambia, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone in Paper 2, because they apply only to candidates of those countries. Preamble and examination scheme summarised in examFormat; suggested reading list skipped.

topics.name: Historiography and Historical Skills
objectives: Explain what history is and why we study it
Identify the sources of history
Apply historical skills (ancient and modern approaches)
Assess the prospects of ICT in historical studies

topics.name: Trans-Saharan Trade
objectives: Trace the origin and organization of the trans-Saharan trade
Assess its effects on the development of West African states

topics.name: Islam in West Africa
objectives: Describe the introduction and spread of Islam in West Africa
Assess the effects of Islam in West Africa

topics.name: European Contact with West Africa
objectives: State the reasons for the coming of Europeans to West Africa
Describe the immediate effects of European contact and the West African reaction

topics.name: Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade
objectives: Trace the origin and organization of the trans-Atlantic slave trade
Assess its effects
Describe its suppression

topics.name: Christian Missionary Activities in West Africa
objectives: Describe the suppression of the slave trade
Assess Christian missionary activities and their impact on West Africa

topics.name: The Scramble for and Partition of West Africa
objectives: Explain the Industrial Revolution and the scramble for colonies
Describe colonial subjugation, occupation and the West African reaction

topics.name: Colonial Rule in West Africa
objectives: Describe the patterns of colonial rule
Explain the consolidation of European culture in Africa
Explain the colonial economy and the underdevelopment of Africa
Assess the impact of the two World Wars on colonial Africa

topics.name: Problems of Independent West African States
objectives: Describe the nature of politics, neo-colonialism and economic underdevelopment
Explain unequal development within states and instability
Assess the role of the military in West African politics
Explain boundary disputes and the threat to West African unity

topics.name: West Africa and International Organizations
objectives: Describe the membership, aims and objectives, achievements and failures of the United Nations Organization (UNO)
Describe the membership, aims and objectives, achievements and failures of the Organization of African Unity (OAU)/African Union (AU)
Describe the membership, aims and objectives, achievements and failures of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
topics.content: United Nations Organization (UNO)/United Nations (UN); Organization of African Unity (OAU)/African Union (AU); Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS); etc. Membership, aims and objectives, achievements and failures.

topics.name: Historiography and Historical Skills (Nigeria)

Identify the sources of history
Apply historical skills (ancient and modern approaches)
Assess the prospects of ICT in historical studies

topics.name: Land and Peoples of Nigeria

Assess the impact of the environment on human activities, e.g. hunting, fishing and farming

topics.name: Centres of Ancient Civilization in Nigeria
objectives: Describe the ancient civilizations of Nok, Ife, Igbo Ukwu and Benin

topics.name: Centralized and Non-Centralized States
topics.content: Centralized and non-centralized states: Kanem and Borno; Hausa; Nupe; Oyo; Benin; Igbo; Efik; Tiv. Inter-group relations: economic activities, intermarriages, bilingualism, etc. Impact of migrations, wars and politics on inter-group relations.

subtopics.name: States and Kingdoms of Nigeria

subtopics.name: Inter-Group Relations
objectives: Explain inter-group relations: economic activities, intermarriages, bilingualism, etc.

subtopics.name: Impact of Migrations, Wars and Politics
objectives: Assess the impact of migrations, wars and politics on inter-group relations

topics.name: Indigenous Crafts and Industries
objectives: Describe the technology of pottery, salt making, iron working, gold mining, soap making, leather works, weaving, carving, bronze casting, tie and dyeing, bead making and boat building

topics.name: External Influences on Nigeria Before 1800

subtopics.name: Early European Contact with Coastal States

objectives: Trace the origin and organization of the trans-Atlantic slave trade in Nigeria
Assess its effects

The Second Phase of the British Conquest of Nigeria, 1900-1960
topics.content: The early phase 1900-1914: the amalgamation of 1914 and its significance. The later phase 1914-1960: central administration; indirect rule; the colonial economy; social developments.

subtopics.name: The Later Phase, 1914-1960
